issues.claim: The company reports leachate COD of 3,400 mg/L. Zorić's zeolite-barrier study addresses ammonium-laden leachate, not demonstrated COD treatment.

sources.quote: our last sampling showed COD at 3,400 mg/L
Permeable reactive barriers (PRBs) using natural zeolite (clinoptilolite) represent an inexpensive passive remediation option for ammonium-laden leachate plumes in alluvial aquifers.

issues.explanation: Jev rates the support of this fact by its source sentences at 0.32. Keep in the fact only what the source states; move any condition, requirement or next step into proposedActions or questions.

issues.claim: the upper 95% uncertainty bound on outward contaminant mass flux across the eastern boundary is no greater than zero in every agreed seasonal scenario

sources.quote: We do not know how far the contamination has moved or which direction groundwater flows under the site at different seasons.
The liner under that area was never designed for liquid retention.

issues.explanation: An east-only flux gate could pass if groundwater or an intervention carries contamination toward another boundary, despite continuing uncontrolled migration. Require the containment gate to cover a locally justified control surface encompassing all plausible downgradient pathways under the agreed seasonal scenarios, rather than the eastern boundary alone.

checklist.evidence: Verified facts: "The company reports seepage toward its boundary and says the yard liner was not designed for liquid retention." and "The company reports leachate COD of 3,400 mg/L."; Proposed next steps: "Four-well installation, submission and professional approvals must also be feasible by the verified deadline." These identify the leaking yard, measured pollution burden and specific regulatory deliverables rather than a generic remediation goal.

Verified facts: "The company reports no dedicated research budget and no laboratory beyond its basic leachate-monitoring wet-chemistry bench."; Proposed next steps: "Cost external analysis, drilling, treatment engineering and sign-off before procurement." and "Agree funding, operating responsibilities and residual disposal."; Open questions: "What is the current order status, verified deadline, inspectorate acceptance process, required sign-offs and applicable monitoring, containment and discharge criteria?" and "Can Zorić confirm availability, field-team capacity and interest in this joint project for the actual delivery period?" These make funding, external capacity, staffing and the historical four-well deadline verifiable prerequisites rather than assumed resources or delivery commitments.

Verified facts: "Zorić's research combines leachate-indicator sampling with transport modelling." and "Her transfer-station study reports a risk: mean-annual containment designs may underestimate peak infiltration by up to 40% in that climatic setting."; Our inference: "Published alluvial-aquifer parameters and ammonium-removal results are not validation for this yard."; Proposed next steps: "Separate tuning batches from held-out collection batches and calibration observations from held-out field measurements; check independence." These connect her documented field and modelling methods to local validation while retaining the reported seasonal limitation and the distinction between ammonium evidence and COD treatment.

Proposed next steps: "The company would supply records, access and actual yard leachate; Zorić would lead surveyed water levels, borehole interpretation, quality-controlled sampling and modelling, with treatment-engineering support." and "Before starting, agree candidate treatments, operating ranges, replication and untreated controls with a treatment engineer."; Our inference: "Openness to joint work does not constitute acceptance of this project." These identify proposed company, researcher and external-engineering contributions without presenting them as confirmed commitments.

Proposed next steps: "Run a field-and-bench feasibility experiment after agreeing the screening and acceptance protocol."; "Compare untreated split-batch controls with individually applied treatments; measure COD, ammonium, residuals and analytical uncertainty."; "Separate tuning batches from held-out collection batches and calibration observations from held-out field measurements; check independence. Select the best configuration using tuning data."; "Before starting, agree candidate treatments, operating ranges, replication and untreated controls with a treatment engineer." These specify inputs, an untreated baseline, treatment comparisons and independent evaluation, with unresolved execution choices explicitly required before starting.

Proposed next steps: "Proposed acceptance unit: each independent collection batch, averaging technical repeats; require its one-sided 95% upper confidence bound, incorporating analytical uncertainty, below every applicable effluent limit, without pooling away failures." This defines treatment acceptance, but the containment gate—"the upper 95% uncertainty bound on outward contaminant mass flux across the eastern boundary is no greater than zero in every agreed seasonal scenario"—covers only the eastern boundary and could pass while contamination migrates in another direction; acceptance covering all locally plausible downgradient pathways is missing.

Proposed next steps: "Compare untreated split-batch controls with individually applied treatments" and "Separate tuning batches from held-out collection batches and calibration observations from held-out field measurements; check independence."; Our inference: "Published alluvial-aquifer parameters and ammonium-removal results are not validation for this yard."; Proposed next steps: "predictions of zero flux alone cannot establish containment." These support controlled treatment screening without asserting that published parameters, fitted models or untested field interventions establish causal containment performance.

Our inference: "Four wells and one campaign would likely leave seasonal reversals or complex plume pathways unresolved; local observations and actual-leachate tests would be needed." and "current researcher availability is unknown, and the historical deadline cannot establish a current delivery schedule."; Proposed next steps: "Missing limits, inadequate validation, insufficient seasonal evidence or unresolved feasibility mean no pass and a revised investigation plan." These name the principal transfer, seasonal, validation and execution risks and keep unresolved conditions open.

Our inference: "This proposal is conditional: current researcher availability is unknown" and "Openness to joint work does not constitute acceptance of this project."; Open questions: "Can Zorić confirm availability, field-team capacity and interest in this joint project for the actual delivery period?" These preserve the distinction between documented openness to collaboration and unconfirmed participation or availability.

Potential benefits: "The experiment could distinguish viable containment and COD-treatment options from unsuitable transfers of published methods, while identifying evidence gaps in a regulator-facing remediation package." and "Conditional on agreement and access, Zorić could test how seasonal gradients and site stratigraphy affect containment design, using yard observations and actual-leachate treatment results." These describe plausible feasibility-study gains for both parties without guaranteeing implementation, regulatory acceptance or research outcomes.
